goal: Test whether exact cross-core information can reduce recipient-core work enough to pay for donor-core work; dual-core existence alone is not a success criterion.

successor_mechanics.ORBIT_INCREMENTAL: Replace independent random powmod probes with a stateful group walk that reuses modular multiplications; collisions still require exact order/factor certification. Must be compared against BSGS and rho-like baselines.
successor_mechanics.RELATION_SCOUT: Run a polynomial-in-bitlength capped congruence-of-squares scout before escalation; scout failure is UNKNOWN and triggers fallback, never a factor absence claim.
successor_mechanics.EARLY_COLLISION_FACTOR: When ORBIT obtains an exact-certified exponent multiple d with a^d=1 mod N, try bounded exact gcd factor extraction from divisors/halves of d before full minimal-order reduction. Any returned factor must divide N exactly.
successor_mechanics.KEYMASTER_ROUTING: Core activation may be sequential/adaptive. Total compute includes all work already spent. Switching is allowed; forgetting donor cost is forbidden.
successor_mechanics.SPIDER_CROSS_CORE_GRAPH: Only exact-certified relations may become cross-core edges; heuristic similarity may rank but not certify.

mad_lab_joint_hardness.objective: Find semiprimes where relation scout exhausts its budget, ORBIT incremental collision remains expensive, and BSGS/rho stay competitive or superior.

future_frozen_gates: exact factor/order correctness on all returned results
total compute beats best successful single constituent on >=25% fresh cases
median total compute no worse than min(BSGS,rho-like strong baseline) on fresh scale ladder
no core's work omitted from total compute
fitted finite-ladder slope reported but never promoted to asymptotic theorem
polynomial_factoring_boundary: No polynomial-time factoring claim is allowed unless worst-case bit complexity, including both cores, switching, verification, memory and all intermediate representations, is formally proved poly(n) for n=ceil(log2 N).
